items.question: How does the backpropagation algorithm compute gradients across network layers?
items.expected_answer: The backpropagation algorithm computes gradients of a scalar loss function with respect to all trainable network weights by recursively applying the multivariate chain rule across nodes of a computational graph, propagating errors backward layer by layer from output activations to input features.
items.evidence: The backpropagation algorithm computes the exact mathematical gradients of a scalar loss function with respect to all trainable network weights by recursively applying the multivariate chain rule across the nodes of a computational graph. Errors are propagated backward layer by layer from output activations to input features, enabling efficient reverse-mode automatic differentiation in deep neural architectures.
items.notes: Direct factual question on backprop chain rule mechanism.

items.question: What are the three fundamental semantic categories defined in Natural Language Inference (NLI)?
items.expected_answer: Natural Language Inference (NLI) classifies the semantic relationship between a premise text and a hypothesis proposition into three fundamental categories: entailment, contradiction, and neutral.
items.evidence: Natural Language Inference (NLI) classifies the semantic relationship between a premise text and a hypothesis proposition into three fundamental categories: entailment, contradiction, and neutral.
items.notes: Exact definition and taxonomy of NLI relationships.

items.question: Why does scaled dot-product attention divide query-key dot products by the square root of the key dimension?
items.expected_answer: Dividing query-key dot products by the square root of the key dimension counteracts exponential magnitude growth in high-dimensional vector spaces, preventing the softmax function from being pushed into regions with near-zero vanishing gradients.
items.evidence: The dot products between query and key vectors are explicitly divided by the square root of the key dimension to counteract exponential magnitude growth in high-dimensional vector spaces, which would otherwise push the softmax function into regions with near-zero vanishing gradients.
items.notes: Conceptual and mathematical explanation of attention scaling.

items.question: How do the latency and discrimination trade-offs between bi-encoders and cross-encoders relate to information retrieval evaluation metrics like Mean Reciprocal Rank?
items.expected_answer: Bi-encoders encode queries and passages independently for sub-millisecond approximate nearest-neighbor retrieval, while cross-encoders perform full token cross-attention for sharper relevance discrimination at higher latency; ranking quality across both is evaluated by metrics such as Mean Reciprocal Rank (MRR), which measures the reciprocal of the rank position of the first relevant retrieved passage.
items.evidence: Page 6: In modern neural information retrieval, bi-encoders encode queries and document passages independently into isolated dense vector representations... Conversely, cross-encoders concatenate the query and candidate passage... sharper relevance discrimination at the cost of higher per-query inference latency. Page 8: Mean Reciprocal Rank (MRR) evaluates the reciprocal of the rank position of the first relevant retrieved passage averaged across all queries.
items.notes: Multi-page synthesis spanning passage 6 (encoder architectures) and passage 8 (ranking metrics).

items.question: What is the primary difference between supervised learning and unsupervised learning in terms of training targets?
items.expected_answer: Supervised learning algorithms optimize predictive models using explicit pairs of input features and ground-truth target labels, whereas unsupervised learning algorithms discover latent structures, cluster partitions, and manifold representations without external supervisory guidance or target labels.
items.evidence: Supervised learning algorithms optimize parametric predictive models using explicit pairs of input features and ground-truth target labels... In contrast, unsupervised learning algorithms discover latent structures, cluster partitions, and manifold representations without external supervisory guidance or target labels.
items.notes: Comparative conceptual question evaluating learning paradigms.

items.question: What is the exact derivative of the Rectified Linear Unit (ReLU) activation function for all positive inputs?
items.expected_answer: The derivative of the Rectified Linear Unit (ReLU) activation function is a constant 1 for all positive inputs.
items.evidence: The Rectified Linear Unit (ReLU) activation function mitigates the vanishing gradient problem in deep multilayer perceptrons because its derivative is a constant 1 for all positive inputs, preventing the exponential gradient decay observed in saturating activation functions...
items.notes: Exact numerical constant evaluation testing precise factual extraction.

items.question: How do Convolutional Neural Networks exploit spatial hierarchies in image grids?
items.expected_answer: CNNs exploit local spatial geometry and translation invariance through weight sharing and localized receptive field convolution kernels, with subsampling and pooling layers compressing spatial dimensions while expanding channel capacity from low-level edges to semantic object representations.
items.evidence: Convolutional Neural Networks (CNNs) exploit the local spatial geometry and translation invariance of image grids through weight sharing and localized receptive field convolution kernels. Subsampling and pooling layers progressively compress spatial dimensions while hierarchically expanding channel feature capacity from low-level edges to semantic object representations.
items.notes: Direct factual question on CNN architecture mechanisms.
